h1: The 8 Best Bagless Self-Emptying Robot Vacuums of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Bagless Self-Empty Robot Vacuums: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 8 bagless self-emptying robot vacuums from Shark, roborock, uninell and Tikom, scored on bin size, mapping and cost.
summary: The Shark AV2501S is the best bagless self-emptying robot, with a 30 day HEPA base, Matrix Clean mapping and a pet hair focus. The roborock Q7 M5+ lists the longest interval, up to 7 to 9 weeks, plus a mop. The Q10 S5+ and uninell cover mid budgets, while Navigators, Airzeen and Tikom fill the simpler and cheaper end.
intro: Self-emptying docks come in two flavors, and the cheaper-to-own one is not the one most people assume. Bagged docks trade your emptying chore for a stream of replacement bags. Bagless docks avoid the recurring cost by collecting debris in a reusable bin, but they move the job: you tip the bin into the trash yourself and wash the filter now and then.

That tradeoff makes bin interval and filtration more important than headline suction. We went through eight bagless models, comparing what each listing says about bin capacity, sealing, navigation and mopping. A mop adds a tank, a pad and a cleaning step; vacuum-only models skip all three. Scores come from spec sheets and owner feedback, with interval and filtration weighed ahead of raw Pa figures.

products.name: Shark AV2501S AI Ultra Robot Vacuum with Matrix Clean, Bagless Self-Empty Base
products.verdict: A 30 day HEPA bagless base, Matrix Clean mapping and a pet hair focus.
products.description:
The Shark AV2501S puts the filtration where it counts. Its bagless base lists a 30 day interval with HEPA sealing, so the dust that goes into the bin stays there until you tip it. Matrix Clean mapping plans coverage rather than bouncing at random, a pet hair focus targets what fills a bin fastest, and an app over Wi-Fi handles control. It sits in the $200 to $500 bracket.

It outranks the roborock Q7 M5+ because the Q7 lists a longer interval but not the filtration detail, and a bagless bin is emptied by hand, which is exactly when sealing matters.

Choose it for a pet household that wants mapping and a clean emptying process. The caveats are real: 30 days is the shortest window among the better models, and it has no mop, so hard-floor owners who want wet cleaning need a second tool.
products.idealFor: Pet homes that want clean, bagless emptying.
products.skipIf: You want mopping in the same machine.

products.name: roborock Q7 M5+ Robot Vacuum and Mop, Up to 7-9 Weeks Self-Empty, 10000Pa
products.verdict: Up to 7 to 9 weeks between empties, 10,000Pa and a mop.
products.description:
The roborock Q7 M5+ wins on interval. Its reusable bagless bin is rated at up to 7 to 9 weeks per empty, the longest here, alongside 10,000Pa suction and a vacuum and mop combination. A longer gap means fewer trips to the trash, and no bags to buy.

It ranks second because the AV2501S gives better filtration detail and mapping information, and the Q7's listing is thinner there. It beats the Q10 S5+ below because the Q10 lists no interval at all.

Buy it if you want the longest stretch between chores. The caveat is that the interval is a ceiling: pet hair and dust fill a bin faster, so a house with a dog will not see nine weeks. The mop also adds a tank and pad to clean, and anyone with allergies should look at the Shark first.

products.name: roborock Q10 S5+ Robot Vacuum and Mop, 10,000Pa Suction
products.verdict: 10,000Pa, mopping and a bagless dock for under $300.
products.description:
The Q10 S5+ is the mid-range roborock: 10,000Pa suction, a combined vacuum and mop and a bagless self-empty dock, in the $200 to $500 bracket. Because the dock uses a reusable bin, running costs stay low, and roborock is a known name with parts available.

It ranks third since the Q7 M5+ lists a longer interval for a similar price, and the Q10's listing gives no interval or LiDAR detail at all. That missing information puts it behind the models that state it.

It suits homes with carpet and hard floors that want mopping on a moderate budget. The caveat is the gap in the listing: without a stated interval you cannot plan your emptying, and the mop adds upkeep. Choose it if you like the brand and plan to read the manual for bin timing.
products.idealFor: Mixed floors on a mid budget.
products.skipIf: You want the longest empty window.

products.name: uninell Robot Vacuum and Mop, 7000Pa, LiDAR Self-Empty Station
products.verdict: LiDAR navigation, 7000Pa and a bagless station on a mid budget.
products.description:
The uninell is the cheapest route to LiDAR with a bagless station. It lists LiDAR navigation, 7000Pa suction, a bagless self-empty station and a mop. LiDAR maps with a laser, which usually gives straighter, more consistent coverage than camera or gyroscope mapping, and that matters in a home with several rooms.

It ranks fourth because the brand is far less known than Shark or roborock, so parts and support are open questions. At 7000Pa it is also lower than the roborock pair.

Buy it if you want LiDAR on a mid budget and accept the brand risk. The caveat is service: check the warranty terms and how replacement filters and brushes are sold before committing. If long-term support matters most, the Shark or roborock models are safer, even without LiDAR.

products.name: Shark Navigator Robot Vacuum + Self-Empty Base, Grey, RV2120AE
products.verdict: A vacuum-only Shark with a bagless base and no mop to maintain.
products.description:
The Shark RV2120AE is the plain vacuum. It has a bagless self-empty base and no mop at all, which means one fewer tank, pad and set of parts to clean. The Shark name and a simple setup make it the least fussy robot here, and it lands in the $200 to $500 bracket.

It sits fifth because the AV2501S adds mapping and HEPA, and the Q7 M5+ adds a mop and a longer interval. Next to those, the RV2120AE is the simple pick, and its listing details are brief, with no mapping stated.

Buy it if you already own a mop you like and want a known brand for vacuum duty. The caveat is information: with no interval or filtration spec listed, you are trusting the brand more than the datasheet, which is a fair trade only for modest homes.

products.name: Shark Navigator Robot Vacuum + Self-Empty Base, White, AV2110S
products.verdict: The same Navigator platform in white, usually a little cheaper.
products.description:
The AV2110S is the same Navigator platform in white. It is a vacuum-only Shark with a bagless self-empty base, and it is usually priced slightly below the grey RV2120AE it shadows. Nothing in the specs separates the two except the finish.

It ranks sixth by a hair: because it is a near twin of the model above, the choice comes down to which is cheaper on the day you buy. If they cost the same, the finish is the only deciding factor.

Pick it for a vacuum-only home where price is the guide and you like the white shell. The caveat mirrors its sibling: no mopping, sparse listing details and no mapping stated. A larger home should look to the AV2501S, whose mapping prevents the missed strips you get from a simple pattern.
products.skipIf: You want a different feature set.

products.name: Airzeen Bagless Robot Vacuum and Mop Self-Emptying for Pet Hair, Carpet
products.verdict: Marketed at pet hair and carpet, with a bagless dock and a mop.
products.description:
The Airzeen is aimed squarely at pet hair and carpet. It is a vacuum and mop combo with a bagless self-emptying base, positioned for the two jobs where bagless docks struggle most. Hair is what clogs a bin path first, so the focus is a fair target, and it sells in the $200 to $500 bracket.

It ranks seventh because the brand is new and the listing gives few specifics. Shark and roborock both have longer records and clearer specs, so a claim of pet and carpet performance carries less weight here.

It suits a pet and carpet home on a mid budget. The caveat is proof: hair clogs are unproven on this model, so read owner comments about the bin, brush and filter before buying. Keep the receipt handy, and consider the AV2501S if you can afford the extra.
products.idealFor: Pet and carpet homes on a mid budget.

products.name: Tikom Robot Vacuum and Mop, Robotic Vacuum Cleaner with Self-Emptying Base
products.verdict: The lowest price here, with a bagless base and a mop.
products.description:
Tikom takes last place, but also the cheapest ticket. It bundles a vacuum and mop with a bagless self-emptying base and app control, at the lowest price in this comparison. For a first robot, that is a low-risk way to see whether a dock suits your home.

It ranks eighth because the listing gives no suction number, interval or mapping detail, and the brand is less established than Shark or roborock. You get the format without the specifications that let you compare it.

Buy it for a first robot on a tight budget. The caveat is that you should expect a lighter feature set and thinner support. If you plan to keep the machine for years, one of the established brands higher up will likely cost less over time.
products.idealFor: First-time buyers on a tight budget.

whatMatters.factor: How a bagless bin is emptied
whatMatters.detail: A bagless dock stores dust in a reusable bin that you tip into the trash. That saves money on bags but can release dust at the moment you empty it. Look for HEPA or sealed in the listing, and plan to empty the bin near a trash can or outdoors, especially if anyone in the house has allergies or asthma.

whatMatters.factor: Interval claims depend on your home
whatMatters.detail: An interval such as 7 to 9 weeks assumes light debris, and pet hair fills a bin far faster. Treat the figure as a ceiling and shorten it for houses with pets or heavy shedding. Compare the stated interval with your household before trusting it, and note which listings give none, since a missing interval is itself a warning.

Bagless docks use washable filters that clog over time and cut suction. Check that the filter is easy to reach, that replacements are sold, and that the manual gives a cleaning schedule. Plan to rinse it about monthly if you have pets, and let it dry fully before reinstalling it, because a damp filter clogs fast and can smell.

A combo adds a water tank and a mop pad, which means more parts to rinse and dry after every run. If you already own a mop you like, a vacuum-only robot such as the Navigators has fewer parts to maintain. Check the listing for the words vacuum and mop to see which you are buying, since the names alone can be misleading.

LiDAR or camera mapping plans straight rows and remembers rooms, while basic robots bounce around and cover less. Mapping matters most in homes with several rooms or furniture clusters. Look for LiDAR or Matrix Clean in the title, and note that the vacuum-only Navigators list no mapping at all, so they suit small homes.

faq.q: What is a bagless self-emptying robot vacuum?
faq.a: It is a robot whose dock pulls debris into a reusable bin instead of a paper bag. You empty the bin by hand every few weeks and wash the filter periodically, so the chore is smaller, not gone.

faq.q: Are bagless docks cheaper to run?
faq.a: Yes, because there are no bags to buy, so running cost is close to nothing. You do need to wash the filter occasionally and replace it eventually, which costs far less than constant bag refills over several years.

faq.q: Is the Shark AV2501S worth more than the Navigator?
faq.a: For pets and larger homes, yes: the AV2501S adds Matrix Clean mapping and a HEPA sealed base. For a single room, a Navigator such as the RV2120AE is enough and costs less money overall.
Listings range from 30 days on the Shark AV2501S to 7 to 9 weeks on the roborock Q7 M5+. Pets and heavy debris shorten that, so treat the weeks as a maximum, not a promise.
They can when you tip the bin. A HEPA sealed design like the Shark AV2501S reduces it, and emptying the bin close to a trash can helps keep dust off the floor and out of the air you breathe.

faq.q: Is the white Navigator different from the grey one?
faq.a: They share the same Navigator platform, so the choice is finish and price. The AV2110S is white and usually slightly cheaper, and the RV2120AE is grey; buy whichever costs less on the day you order.

finalTake: The Shark AV2501S is the pick for pet homes that want sealed, mapped, bagless emptying. Choose the roborock Q7 M5+ for the longest gap between chores, and the Q10 S5+ for a mid budget with mopping. The uninell is the cheapest LiDAR route, and the Navigators, Airzeen and Tikom suit buyers who can accept thinner specs.
